hero.title: Seabourn Arctic and Greenland Cruises
hero.subtitle: Svalbard, Glaciers & Polar Wildlife
paragraphs: A Seabourn Arctic and Greenland cruise offers an opportunity to explore some of the most remote landscapes in the Northern Hemisphere while traveling aboard a purpose-built luxury expedition ship.

From the glacier-carved fjords of Greenland to the dramatic wilderness of Svalbard, Seabourn's Arctic expeditions combine wildlife viewing, Zodiac exploration, guided walks, cultural experiences and expert-led interpretation with the comfort of an ultra-luxury ship.

Depending on the itinerary, voyages can also include Iceland, the Canadian Arctic, Baffin Island, Ellesmere Island and the Northwest Passage. Seabourn's current Arctic program includes voyages aboard Seabourn Venture and Seabourn Pursuit, with itineraries varying by season and year.

This guide explains where Seabourn goes in the Arctic, what you can see, what expedition activities are included, when to travel, what to pack and whether a Seabourn Arctic or Greenland cruise is right for you.

whyTakeSection.title: Why Take a Seabourn Arctic Cruise?
whyTakeSection.subtitle: WHY GO
paragraphs: The Arctic is one of the world's great wilderness destinations.
The expedition format allows travelers to experience the landscape at close range through Zodiac cruises, shore landings and guided walks.
Seabourn describes its Arctic experience as a combination of remote exploration and luxury, with expert Expedition Teams providing interpretation throughout the voyage.
whyTakeSection.conclusion: Instead of traveling between conventional ports, a Seabourn expedition takes you into pristine polar environments defined by raw wilderness and effortless residential comfort.

destinationsShowcase.title: Seabourn Greenland & Svalbard Cruises
destinationsShowcase.subtitle: THE TWO ICONS OF THE ARCTIC

items.title: Greenland Expedition Cruises
items.subtitle: Seabourn Greenland Cruises
items.description: Greenland is one of the highlights of Seabourn's Arctic program. Its immense landscapes include glaciers, icebergs, deep fjords, mountainous coastlines, tundra, remote settlements and Arctic wildlife. A Greenland expedition provides a very different experience from a conventional cruise — it is about landscape, wildlife, culture and exploration rather than shopping or traditional sightseeing.
items.bestFor: Glacier viewing, Zodiac cruising, shore walks, remote villages, cultural encounters, wildlife observation, and scenic fjord cruising. Seabourn specifically highlights Greenland's fjords and the cultural traditions of communities that have long lived in these northern environments.

items.category: High Arctic Sea Ice & Polar Wildlife
items.title: Svalbard Expedition Cruises
items.subtitle: Seabourn Svalbard Cruises
items.description: Svalbard is one of the most compelling destinations for Arctic expedition travelers. The Norwegian archipelago lies far north of mainland Europe and is known for sea ice, glaciers, Arctic mountains, remote beaches, polar wildlife and long summer daylight. Svalbard offers one of the best opportunities to experience a true High Arctic environment without traveling to the geographic North Pole.
items.bestFor: Glacier fronts, sea ice navigation, mountainous islands, coastal tundra, and polar bear habitats. Seabourn's Arctic program includes Svalbard expeditions designed to explore the archipelago in greater depth, spending multiple days navigating according to ice and wildlife conditions.

wildlifeSection.title: Seabourn Arctic Wildlife
wildlifeSection.subtitle: NATIVE SPECIES
paragraphs: Wildlife is one of the biggest reasons travelers choose Arctic expeditions. Seabourn emphasizes wildlife viewing throughout its Arctic itineraries, while noting that sightings depend on local conditions and the animals themselves.

items.title: Polar Bears
items.description: For many travelers, the polar bear is the ultimate Arctic wildlife encounter. Polar bears can be found in several Arctic regions, including areas around Svalbard and the Canadian Arctic.
features: Pack ice and floe edge habitats
Svalbard & High Arctic Canada
Expert scouting by expedition team
Observed from safe ship and Zodiac distances
Influenced by sea ice and seal movements

items.title: Walrus & Seal Viewing
items.description: Walruses can sometimes be found hauled out on beaches or ice floes. Seals are also common Arctic wildlife, with several species inhabiting polar waters.
features: Atlantic walrus haul-outs on beaches
Ringed, bearded, and harp seals
Sea-level Zodiac exploration
Close approaches while maintaining distance
Pristine coastal ice habitats

items.title: Whale Watching & Marine Life
items.description: Depending on the itinerary and season, travelers may encounter whales in Arctic waters while cruising in Greenland, Iceland, and polar fjords.
features: Beluga whales & narwhals
Minke, humpback, and fin whales
Bowhead whales in High Arctic waters
Spontaneous fjord sightings from verandas
Acrobatic feeding behavior near glacier fronts

zodiacTabs.subtitle: GETTING CLOSER
zodiacTabs.description: Zodiac exploration and guided shore walks are central to the Seabourn Arctic experience, taking guests off the ship to experience polar wilderness at close range aboard purpose-built expedition craft.

tabs.label: Zodiac Excursions
tabs.title: Seabourn Arctic Zodiac Excursions
tabs.description: Zodiac exploration is central to the Seabourn Arctic experience. Seabourn's purpose-built expedition ships carry 24 Zodiacs and are designed for exploration in challenging polar environments.
features: Cruise alongside massive glaciers
Explore narrow waterways and rocky fjords
Search for marine wildlife and polar bears
Approach remote inaccessible coastlines
Visit untouched gravel beaches
Reach shore landing sites safely
View sea ice and icebergs from sea level

tabs.label: Zodiac Landings
tabs.title: What Is a Seabourn Zodiac Landing Like?
tabs.description: A Zodiac landing is different from stepping off a ship at a conventional cruise terminal. Landing locations adapt to weather, sea conditions, ice floes, and wildlife safety.
features: Board Zodiacs directly from the ship's sheltered platform
Travel toward a remote wilderness landing site
Step ashore with direct assistance from the Expedition Team
Explore the area through guided walks or hikes
Return safely to the ship for warm beverages

tabs.label: Guided Walks & Hikes
tabs.title: Arctic Guided Walks and Hikes
tabs.description: Walking ashore is an essential part of the expedition experience. Walks range from gentle scenic strolls to active tundra and ridge hikes led by armed expedition guides.

Remote gravel beaches and driftwood shores
Historic trapper cabins and whaling stations
Authentic Inuit villages and settlements
Panoramic mountain and fjord viewpoints
Nesting seabird cliffs and reindeer habitats

tabs.label: Ice Landings

Viewing towering blue icebergs up close
Navigating close to thunderous glacier fronts
Experiencing frozen polar seas firsthand
Guided by experienced ice masters and glaciologists

expeditionTeam.title: Seabourn Arctic Expedition Team
expeditionTeam.subtitle: EXPERT GUIDANCE
expeditionTeam.description: The Expedition Team is an essential pillar of every polar voyage. Comprising up to 24 world-renowned specialists, they provide daily briefings, lectures, wildlife interpretation, shore guidance, safety instructions and cultural context.

roles.title: Naturalists & Marine Biologists
roles.description: Provide deep wildlife interpretation, lead Zodiac wildlife scouting, and deliver daily briefings on polar bears, whales, seals, and Arctic ecosystems.

roles.title: Historians & Geologists
roles.description: Offer rich cultural context on Inuit heritage, heroic age polar exploration, Arctic archaeology, and the dynamic geology of tectonic fjords.

roles.title: Glaciologists & Photographers
roles.description: Explain ice dynamics and climate science while providing hands-on camera guidance to help guests capture breathtaking polar imagery.

cultureSection.heading: Arctic Cultural Experiences
cultureSection.subtitle: THE HUMAN SIDE OF THE ARCTIC
paragraphs: An Arctic cruise isn't only about ice and wildlife. The region has long been home to communities with deep relationships to the land and sea.
Greenland's history adds another dimension to the journey — travelers may encounter communities where traditional Arctic culture remains closely connected to the surrounding environment.
highlights: Remote Inuit village visits and authentic community interactions
Traditional storytelling, oral histories, and legends
Cultural interpretation by local guides and elders
Historic archaeological sites, turf houses, and Norse ruins
Local Arctic art, crafts, and stone carvings
Discussions about modern life and sustainable living in the High Arctic

northernLights.title: Seabourn Arctic and Northern Lights
northernLights.subtitle: CHASING THE AURORA
paragraphs: The Northern Lights can be one of the most spectacular possibilities on an Arctic voyage. However, seeing the aurora is never guaranteed — it depends on solar activity, darkness, cloud cover, location and weather.
Seabourn highlights opportunities to search for the Northern Lights from the ship, including specialized observation areas such as the panoramic Constellation Lounge and open outdoor decks.

Can you see the Northern Lights on a Greenland cruise? Potentially, but travelers should understand the aurora is a natural phenomenon rather than a scheduled activity. Later summer departures (August-September) offer increasing hours of nighttime darkness optimal for aurora viewing.

seasonsTimeline.title: Best Time for a Seabourn Arctic Cruise
seasonsTimeline.subtitle: ARCTIC CRUISE SEASONS EXPLAINED

items.title: Early Season (April – June)
items.description: Cooler polar conditions, extensive sea ice, dramatic snow-capped landscapes, and a strong expedition atmosphere. Ideal for ice navigation and wildlife on sea ice.

items.title: Mid-Season (July – August)
items.description: 24-hour Midnight Sun daylight, maximum ice melt allowing deeper fjord access, active wildlife viewing (seabirds, whales, polar bears), and extensive shore exploration time.

items.title: Late Season (August – September)
items.description: Changing autumn tundra colors, shifting wildlife migration patterns, and returning dark evening skies providing potential opportunities to search for the Northern Lights.

items.title: Seabourn Venture
items.subtitle: Arctic, Greenland & Northwest Passage

Its PC6 Polar Class ice-strengthened hull is engineered for Svalbard, Greenland, Iceland, the Canadian Arctic, and the Northwest Passage. experienceNeeded.title: Do You Need Polar Expedition Experience?
experienceNeeded.subtitle: GETTING READY & PHYSICAL PREPARATION
paragraphs: No. You don't need previous polar expedition experience to enjoy a Seabourn Arctic cruise. The Expedition Team guides and assists guests throughout every stage of the voyage.

However, you should be comfortable with the realities of expedition travel. Activity levels vary by excursion — the ability to step into and out of Zodiacs and walk on uneven natural terrain is important.
highlights: Zodiac boarding and stepping ashore onto uneven rocky beaches
Walking on natural tundra, loose gravel, and unpaved terrain
Cold, breezy, or wet polar weather conditions
Flexible daily schedules that adapt to ice and wildlife opportunities
Following safety protocols set by armed expedition guides
experienceNeeded.conclusion: With dedicated crew assistance, first-time expedition cruisers regularly enjoy every aspect of Seabourn's Arctic itineraries in total comfort and safety.

bookingTips.title: Tips for Booking a Seabourn Arctic Cruise
bookingTips.subtitle: BEFORE YOU BOOK • EXPERT EXPEDITION GUIDANCE

items.title: Choose the Destination Before the Ship
items.description: Decide whether you most want Greenland's fjords, Svalbard's High Arctic sea ice, Iceland's volcanism, or the historic Northwest Passage before choosing sailing dates.

items.title: Compare the Seasons Carefully
items.description: Early season (June) brings dramatic sea ice; mid-season (July-August) offers 24-hour daylight and active whales; late season (August-September) brings autumn tundra and potential Northern Lights.

items.title: Look at the Total Expedition Days
items.description: Longer itineraries (14 to 24 days) offer substantially more opportunities for spontaneous wildlife encounters and remote fjord exploration.

items.title: Review Excursion Activity Levels
items.description: Ensure you are comfortable with Zodiac boarding from the platform and walking on unpaved gravel and tundra terrain.

items.title: Choose Your Suite Category Carefully
items.description: A private veranda suite provides priceless impromptu viewing when whales or polar bears appear alongside the ship.

items.title: Pack for Layering and Flexibility
items.description: High-performance thermal base layers, waterproof outer shells, and warm gloves are far more effective than bulky single coats.

items.title: Bring High-Quality Binoculars
items.description: A quality pair of 8x42 or 10x42 binoculars is the single most valuable piece of gear for spotting polar bears, walruses, and seabirds.

items.title: Work with a Polar Travel Specialist
items.description: A knowledgeable luxury advisor helps compare routes, reserve prime suites, coordinate charter flights to Longyearbyen/Kangerlussuaq, and secure VIP amenities.

faqs.question: What is a Seabourn Arctic cruise?
faqs.answer: A Seabourn Arctic cruise is a luxury expedition voyage exploring remote northern destinations such as Greenland, Svalbard, Iceland and the Canadian Arctic.

faqs.question: Does Seabourn cruise to Greenland?
faqs.answer: Yes. Greenland is an important destination within Seabourn's Arctic expedition program. Current and future itineraries include Greenland and its fjords and remote northern landscapes.

faqs.question: Does Seabourn cruise to Svalbard?
faqs.answer: Yes. Seabourn offers expedition itineraries featuring Svalbard, including voyages designed to explore the archipelago in greater depth.

faqs.question: Which Seabourn ships sail the Arctic?
faqs.answer: Seabourn Venture and Seabourn Pursuit are the company's purpose-built expedition ships used for Arctic exploration.

faqs.question: Can you see polar bears on a Seabourn Arctic cruise?
faqs.answer: Polar bears are among the wildlife travelers may search for in Arctic regions such as Svalbard and the Canadian Arctic. Sightings are never guaranteed.

faqs.question: What other wildlife can you see?
faqs.answer: Possible wildlife includes walruses, seals, beluga whales, other whales, Arctic foxes, muskox, caribou and numerous seabirds.

faqs.question: Are Zodiac excursions included?
faqs.answer: Seabourn's Arctic program includes Zodiac cruises and selected landings as part of the expedition experience. Specific inclusions should always be confirmed for the individual sailing.

faqs.question: Can you go ashore in Greenland?
faqs.answer: Yes. Depending on the itinerary and conditions, guests can participate in shore landings, guided walks and cultural experiences.

faqs.question: Can you see the Northern Lights?
faqs.answer: Potentially. The Northern Lights depend on darkness, solar activity and weather. Seabourn specifically highlights opportunities to search for the aurora on Arctic voyages.

faqs.question: What is the best time for a Seabourn Arctic cruise?
faqs.answer: The main expedition season is during the Arctic's warmer months. Seabourn's current programs include summer Arctic voyages, with exact timing varying by destination and year.

faqs.question: Is Greenland or Svalbard better?
faqs.answer: It depends on your interests. Choose Greenland for immense fjords, glaciers and Arctic communities. Choose Svalbard for High Arctic landscapes, sea ice and strong polar wildlife opportunities.

faqs.question: Is a Seabourn Arctic cruise physically demanding?
faqs.answer: Some excursions can be moderately active, particularly Zodiac boarding, shore landings and hikes. Activity levels vary by excursion.

faqs.question: Do I need previous expedition experience?
faqs.answer: No. Seabourn's Expedition Team guides guests throughout the voyage, making the experience accessible to first-time expedition travelers.

faqs.question: What should I pack for a Seabourn Arctic cruise?
faqs.answer: Bring waterproof outerwear, warm layers, waterproof footwear, gloves, a hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, binoculars and appropriate photography equipment.

faqs.question: Does Seabourn provide expedition gear?
faqs.answer: Selected Seabourn Arctic voyages include expedition items such as a custom parka and waterproof day pack. Guests should check the specific sailing's inclusions before packing.

faqs.question: Is kayaking available?
faqs.answer: Kayaking is available as an optional experience on selected Arctic itineraries.

faqs.question: Is a Seabourn Greenland cruise worth it?
faqs.answer: For travelers who value remote landscapes, wildlife, expedition exploration and luxury service, a Seabourn Greenland cruise can be an excellent choice.

faqs.question: Is Seabourn Arctic better than Antarctica?
faqs.answer: Neither is universally better. The Arctic is especially appealing for Greenland, Svalbard, polar bears and Arctic cultures, while Antarctica is particularly compelling for penguins, ice landscapes and the Antarctic Peninsula.

finalVerdict.title: Remote Wilderness, Delivered in Comfort
finalVerdict.subtitle: OUR SEABOURN ARCTIC VERDICT
paragraphs: Seabourn Arctic and Greenland cruises are an excellent fit for travelers who want to explore the far north in comfort while remaining deeply connected to the landscape. The combination of Svalbard, Greenland, glaciers, sea ice, polar wildlife, Zodiac exploration and Arctic culture creates an experience unlike a conventional luxury cruise.
The biggest appeal is the opportunity to travel into places that are difficult to reach independently while having a purpose-built expedition ship and expert team supporting the journey.
finalVerdict.recommendation: Our recommendation: If your idea of luxury travel includes wildlife, remote landscapes, meaningful cultural experiences and adventure, a Seabourn Arctic or Greenland expedition may be one of the most rewarding choices in the Seabourn portfolio.
